title: Rig Relay Release Candidate Coherence Audit v0
summary: Second holistic audit evaluating Rig Relay's readiness to move toward a release candidate. Assesses the repo across product story, public surface, release boundary, security posture, observability, context governance, runtime safety, desktop golden path, static docs, information architecture, supply chain hygiene, and contribution/business posture. Identifies 10 release blockers, 12 P0 actions, 8 P1 actions, and 11 deferred items for v1.1/v1.2.

scope.description: Full repository release candidate readiness assessment covering product, architecture, security, observability, docs, runtime, supply chain, and public presentation.
in_scope: Product story and public surface (docs/index.html, README.md, static site)
Security posture (threat model, security policy, token handling, WebSocket auth)
Observability and tracing (golden path traces, correlation vocabulary, trace store)
Context assembler and agent governance (code schemas, context assembly, generated content exclusion)
Runtime tool safety (tool permissions, execute_tool_batch, mutation safety, dirty files)
Frontend desktop golden path (bridge server, WebSocket auth, projections)
Static docs renderer (modularization, reproducibility, generated output safety)
Documentation information architecture (collections, navigation, archive vs. homepage)
Supply chain and repo hygiene (dependency pinning, generated files, .gitignore)
Contribution and business posture (AGPL/CLA, licensing clarity, attribution)

findings.title: README is strong but static site homepage doesn't tell the product story
findings.description: The README.md tells a clear product story with Quick Start and demo walkthrough. However, docs/index.html serves as an archive/portal landing page, not a product homepage. The README and the static site diverge in narrative — someone landing on the GitHub Pages site gets an archive index rather than a product introduction.
findings.evidence: docs/index.html has 34 H2s representing collection entries but no product narrative section. README.md has Quick Start, Demo Walkthrough, and clear problem statement. The two surfaces serve different audiences with no bridge.
findings.impact: A non-technical reviewer, partner, or funder landing on the static site cannot quickly understand what Rig Relay does. First impression is an archive, not a product.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a curated homepage section (or separate site_home.v1.json) that presents: (1) one-line problem statement, (2) what works today, (3) audience-appropriate Quick Start, (4) link to archive/evidence. The archive remains accessible but not the first impression.
findings.validation_command: uv run python scripts/render_static_docs.py && grep -c 'Rig Relay' docs/index.html

findings.title: Static site navigation and accessibility are good; missing <nav> landmark and collection landing page
findings.description: The static site passes most accessibility checks: skip link, semantic landmarks (header, main, footer), one H1 per page, focus-visible styles, OG tags, Twitter card, favicon, meta description, lang attribute. However, no <nav> landmark element exists, and docs/collections/index.html is missing (archive split not implemented). The site is presentable but not polished.
findings.evidence: docs/index.html: 34 H2s, skip link present, OG tags present, favicon present, <main> present, lang='en'. No <nav> element. No docs/collections/index.html exists.
findings.impact: Navigation relies on inline H2 lists rather than semantic <nav>. Missing archive collection index page means there's no clear entry point into the archive. WCAG 2.2 navigation landmark compliance is partial.
findings.recommended_fix: Add <nav aria-label='Site navigation'> around the H2 collection listing. Generate docs/collections/index.html as the archive landing page.

findings.title: 8 generated doc pages contain absolute local paths
findings.description: Scan of docs/pages/ reveals 8 HTML files containing absolute paths like /Users/ or /home/. These appear to originate from audit/inventory source JSON files that reference local paths. While not secrets, they leak development machine details.
findings.evidence: Files: docs/pages/fleet-coordination-plane.html (1), docs/pages/declutter-plan.html (1), docs/pages/inventory.html (6), docs/pages/textual-rig-console-slice-5-runtime-provider.html (1), docs/pages/coordination-guard-availability.html (3), docs/pages/bash-deterministic-envelope.html (5), docs/pages/tool-usage-summary.html (5), docs/pages/ide-sidecar-ipc.html (6).
findings.impact: Local path leakage in public static site is a hygiene issue. While threat model (T13) flags this as a release blocker for trace data leakage, the existing instances are development paths, not secrets. Still incompatible with a polished release candidate.
findings.recommended_fix: Add automated local path detection to the renderer validation step. Redact or relativize paths in source JSON docs. Add pre-render scan to the audit support script.

findings.title: 93 generated pages contain token/secret vocabulary — investigation needed
findings.description: A pattern scan of generated HTML for 'token', 'password', 'secret', 'api_key' matches 93 files. However, this includes legitimate pages: security threat model, security policy, privacy notice, and governance docs that discuss tokens and secrets as topics. A deeper scan is needed to separate legitimate usage from actual leaks.
findings.evidence: 93 page files match the pattern. Context: pages include rig-relay-threat-model-v0.html, security_policy_v0.html, privacy-notice-alpha.html, and other security/governance pages where token/secret discussion is expected.
findings.impact: Cannot determine if actual secrets leak without deeper content analysis. Bulk false-positive rate is high but cannot be assumed zero. A release candidate needs a confident answer.
findings.recommended_fix: Run a context-aware scanner that distinguishes: (a) discussions of tokens/secrets from (b) actual token-like strings (high-entropy base64, sk- prefixes). Add this to the audit support script and CI.

findings.title: Release boundary artifacts exist but are alpha-scoped, not v1-scoped
findings.description: docs/json/release/ contains: alpha-release-checklist.v1.json, known-limitations-alpha.v1.json, static_site_v1_readiness.v1.json, and versioning-policy.v1.json. These artifacts frame the release as 'alpha' — there is no v1 release scope document that distinguishes v1 blockers from v1.1/v1.2 debt.
findings.evidence: The 'alpha' framing is consistent across release artifacts. The static_site_v1_readiness doc focuses on docs site only, not the full product. No unified v1 release scope artifact exists.
findings.impact: Without a named v1 scope, it's impossible for a reviewer to determine whether the project considers itself ready. The current artifacts say 'alpha' everywhere.
findings.recommended_fix: Create a v1 release scope document that defines: (a) minimum coherent surface for v1, (b) what's deferred to v1.1/v1.2, (c) acceptance gates. This audit serves as input to that document.

findings.title: Threat model covers 14 assets, 17 threats, 10 trust boundaries — 10 of 17 threats are release blockers still open
findings.description: The threat model (threat_model_v0.v1.json) is comprehensive: 14 assets, 17 threats, 10 trust boundaries, 6 entry points, 6 mitigations, 5 release gates, 5 tests. However, 10 threats are classified as release_blocker=true and all are status=open. Key open blockers: CSWSH (T06), Sensitive Data Exfiltration (T03), Generated Docs Unsafe HTML (T12), Generated Docs Path Leakage (T13).
findings.evidence: T01-T06, T08, T10, T12, T13 are release_blocker=true and status=open. Release gates G01-G04 are release_blocker=true and pending. Mitigations are described but not all tested.
findings.impact: A release candidate cannot ship with 10 open critical/high severity threats that the threat model itself classifies as release blockers. The threat model gate is not passed.
findings.recommended_fix: Close the minimum set of release-blocking threats before v1: (a) WebSocket origin validation (T06/G01), (b) verify no token leakage in traces/docs (T04-T05/G02), (c) verify generated docs HTML safety (T12/G03), (d) verify code schema authority (T14/G04). Defer prompt injection classifier (T01-T02) as acknowledged gap.

findings.title: WebSocket origin validation (CSWSH) is missing — release blocker G01
findings.description: The desktop bridge server does not validate the Origin header on WebSocket upgrade requests. The threat model (T06, G01) classifies this as a release blocker. The server binds to loopback only, which limits attack surface, but a malicious local page or browser extension could exploit this.
findings.evidence: Bridge server auth flow: auth token via query string, auth message validation, handshake_id gating. No Origin header check in _handle_ws or ws_handler. Threat model G01 requires Origin validation.
findings.impact: A malicious page on the same machine could open a WebSocket to the local bridge and receive projection streams if it obtains or bypasses the auth token. Defense-in-depth requires origin validation even on loopback.
findings.recommended_fix: In _handle_ws, validate that the Origin header matches expected loopback origins (http://localhost, http://127.0.0.1, http://localhost:PORT). Reject connections from unexpected origins with 403. Add to bridge_server.py's WebSocket handshake path.

findings.title: Auth token transmitted via query string in WebSocket upgrade
findings.description: The auth token is extracted from the WebSocket URL query string (?token=...). While the connection is loopback and TLS is available, query string tokens appear in server logs, HTTP referrer headers, and browser history. Best practice is to use the WebSocket auth message only, not URL tokens.
findings.evidence: _extract_qs_token() in bridge_server.py extracts token from URL query string. Token is also validated via WebSocket auth message. The QS token is a secondary path that creates unnecessary exposure.
findings.impact: Token in URL increases exposure surface: browser history, proxy logs, and potential referrer leakage if the frontend navigates.
findings.recommended_fix: Use WebSocket auth message as the sole authentication mechanism. Accept token as a Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header or within the first auth message only. Remove QS token extraction path.

findings.title: Golden path trace stages are well-defined; WebSocket security rejection tracing is present
findings.description: rig_relay_trace_golden_path.py defines REQUIRED_STAGES for desktop bridge (9 stages) and FRONTEND_STAGES (6 stages). Bridge server emits golden events throughout the lifecycle. Correlation vocabulary exists (handshake_id). WebSocket rejections emit trace events with reasons. The observability surface is well-architected.
findings.evidence: REQUIRED_STAGES: launch_requested, frontend_resolved, runtime_config_built, server_bound, health_probe_passed, websocket.accepted, websocket.auth_received, websocket.auth_ok, projection.sent. FRONTEND_STAGES: boot_started, runtime_config_loaded, websocket_connecting, auth_ok, projection_received, projection_rendered.
findings.impact: Positive finding. The tracing infrastructure is coherent and sufficient for release candidate observability.
findings.recommended_fix: Continue current trajectory. Consider adding context assembly and tool execution stages to the trace vocabulary for completeness.

findings.title: Context assembly and tool execution stages not yet in golden path trace vocabulary
findings.description: The golden path trace covers desktop bridge and frontend stages well, but context assembly and tool execution paths are not yet traceable through the same vocabulary. For a release candidate, it would strengthen trust to be able to trace a full round-trip: prompt → context assembly → LLM call → tool execution → report.
findings.evidence: REQUIRED_STAGES and FRONTEND_STAGES cover desktop bridge lifecycle. No equivalent stage list for context assembly or tool execution in the golden path tracer.
findings.impact: Low impact for v0 release. Tracing desktop+bridge is sufficient for first release candidate. Context and tool tracing is deferred improvement.
findings.recommended_fix: Add to v1.1 planning. Define context.assembly.* and tool.execution.* trace stages.
findings.deferred_reason: Desktop bridge tracing is sufficient for v0 release candidate. Context/tool tracing is v1.1 scope.

findings.title: Code schema library exists with 7 schemas and authority hashes — router is script-only, not live-integrated
findings.description: 7 code schemas exist in docs/json/code_schemas/ with an index. The router (scripts/rig_relay_select_code_schemas.py) provides CLI-based schema selection with authority hash validation and exclusion patterns. However, the router is script-only — not integrated into the live context assembler. The context_assembler_integration_plan.v1.json code schema exists but its implementation status is unclear.
findings.evidence: Code schemas: context_assembler_integration_plan, desktop_golden_path_trace, frontend_trace_endpoint, frontend_transport_state_reducer, index, json_documentation_migration, tool_batch_execution. Router has _EXCLUDE_CONTEXT_GLOBS including docs/pages/**. Integration is script-only.
findings.impact: Without live integration, the context assembler does not benefit from code schema guidance during agent sessions. The schemas exist but do not yet govern context assembly at runtime.
findings.recommended_fix: Wire the code schema router into the context assembler's candidate selection phase. At minimum, apply exclude patterns at runtime so generated HTML never enters context. Full schema-guided assembly can be v1.1.

findings.title: Generated HTML exclusion patterns exist but are not enforced at runtime
findings.description: The code schema router's _EXCLUDE_CONTEXT_GLOBS correctly excludes docs/pages/**, docs/collections/**, docs/assets/**, **/*.html. However, this is script-level configuration — there is no hard guard in the context assembler that rejects generated HTML paths. Threat T15 explicitly identifies the risk of context assembler selecting generated HTML instead of source JSON.
findings.evidence: Threat T15: 'Context assembler could inadvertently include generated HTML pages as source context.' Missing mitigation: 'Hard guard in context planner against generated HTML paths.' Router's exclude patterns are not runtime-enforced.
findings.impact: If the context assembler discovers docs/pages/*.html files and feeds them as context, the agent receives rendered HTML (potentially escaped, stale, or missing metadata) instead of canonical JSON. This is a context integrity issue.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a hard path-exclusion guard in the context candidate discovery/planning phase that rejects any path matching docs/pages/**, docs/collections/**, **/*.html before candidates enter the assembly pipeline.

findings.title: Tool hardening is well-implemented: env scrubbing, bash rerouting, symlink protection, pattern detection
findings.description: The runtime tool safety infrastructure is robust: sanitize_env_for_subprocess (28 vars), is_likely_binary, resolve_safe_path, bash rerouting, detect_dangerous_bash_patterns, sensitive path blocking. Tool permissions (ALWAYS/ASK/NEVER) and patch gating are in place. execute_tool_batch is single-use with explicit lifecycle.
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md documents all tool hardening measures. Bridge server strips auth_token from HTTP responses. Tool permission gating and PatchGatingMixin are operational.
findings.impact: Positive finding. Tool safety posture is strong for a release candidate. The hardening surface exceeds what many comparable tools ship with.
findings.recommended_fix: Continue current trajectory. Consider adding tool argument schema validation before execution (noted as missing mitigation in T03).

findings.title: Dirty-file preservation policy is well-documented — not validated by automated tests
findings.description: AGENTS.md defines a comprehensive dirty-file preservation policy: protected files, additive edits, no git restore/reset/clean. However, threat T10 (Unsafe File Mutation) has no tests_or_proofs listed. The dirty guard logic should be testable.
findings.evidence: Threat T10 tests_or_proofs: []. Threat T10 is release_blocker=true. Dirty guard exists in governance but lacks automated validation.
findings.impact: Without tests, the dirty-file guard cannot be verified to work correctly under concurrent agent access. This is a gap for a release candidate.
findings.recommended_fix: Add tests that verify: (a) write to dirty file is refused, (b) additive edits on dirty files succeed, (c) collision warnings trigger on cross-lane path conflicts.

findings.title: Desktop WebSocket test collection errors — 6 tests fail to collect
findings.description: Running pytest --collect-only shows 6 collection errors in desktop tests: test_golden_path_browser_integration.py, test_websocket_correlation.py, test_websocket_server.py. These tests cannot be collected, meaning the desktop WebSocket test suite is broken.
findings.evidence: pytest --collect-only output: ERROR tests/desktop/test_golden_path_browser_integration.py, ERROR tests/desktop/test_websocket_correlation.py, ERROR tests/desktop/test_websocket_server.py. 6677 total tests collected, 6 errors.
findings.impact: If the WebSocket server and golden path browser integration tests cannot even collect, the desktop bridge's security path (auth, projection, origin validation) is untested. This directly blocks release candidate since multiple security release blockers involve the WebSocket path.
findings.recommended_fix: Debug and fix the collection errors in the three failing test files. Ensure test_golden_path_browser_integration.py, test_websocket_correlation.py, and test_websocket_server.py collect and pass before release candidate.

findings.title: Renderer is monolithic — no modularization yet
findings.description: The renderer lives entirely in scripts/render_static_docs.py (~1000+ lines). No rig_relay/docs_renderer/ package exists. All concerns (page rendering, collection rendering, homepage, OG tags, breadcrumbs, validation, search index) are in one file.
findings.evidence: No rig_relay/docs_renderer/ directory. All renderer functions are in scripts/render_static_docs.py. The script handles homepage, collections, pages, search index, render manifest in one pass.
findings.impact: Monolithic renderer works correctly and produces consistent output. Modularization is a code-quality concern, not a release blocker. The renderer produces 219 pages with correct metadata and accessibility.
findings.recommended_fix: Defer modularization to post-v0. Current monolith is functionally correct and reproducible. Modularize when adding diagram support or new page types.
findings.deferred_reason: Monolith works. Modularize post-v0 when adding diagram support or new page types.

findings.title: Generated output is reproducible with complete search/render manifests
findings.description: The renderer produces 219 document pages, 33 collection pages, search-index.json (63KB, 219 entries), and render-manifest.json (47KB). Output is deterministic and reproducible. All pages have OG tags, canonical URLs, breadcrumbs, and accessibility features.
findings.evidence: docs/search-index.json: 63017 bytes. docs/render-manifest.json: 47193 bytes. Static site readiness doc confirms 100% migration hash coverage, schema faithfulness, and accessibility checks passing.
findings.impact: Positive finding. The static site infrastructure is release-ready from a technical perspective. The remaining gap is product storytelling (F01), not rendering quality.
findings.recommended_fix: No action needed on rendering. Focus on content/curation improvements (F01, F05).
findings.validation_command: uv run python scripts/render_static_docs.py && diff <(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.dumps(json.load(open("docs/render-manifest.json")), sort_keys=True))') <(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.dumps(json.load(open("docs/render-manifest.json")), sort_keys=True))')

findings.title: 33 collections provide good conceptual organization — security and code schemas are collections
findings.description: The site manifest defines 33 collections organized by concept (Architecture, Audits, Governance, Security, Conversations, Evidence, etc.), not by directory. Both Security and Code Schemas have dedicated collections. Documentation is navigable by concept. 219 documents are catalogued with 0 orphans.
findings.evidence: Site manifest collections include: architecture, audits, code_schemas, conversations, demo, evidence, findings, governance, legal, protocols, publishing, release, security, troubleshooting, ui. Security and code schemas are surfaced as top-level collections.
findings.impact: Positive finding. Information architecture is well-organized for a release candidate. The collection system supports concept-based navigation.
findings.recommended_fix: No action needed. Consider adding a 'Getting Started' collection that bridges README → static site.

findings.title: No diagrams or visual explanations in documentation schema
findings.description: The documentation page schema (rig.documentation.page.v1) supports text blocks (headings, paragraphs, callouts, lists, tables, code, JSON, evidence, links, file-refs) but has no diagram or image block type. Architecture docs are text-only.
findings.evidence: Schema block types: heading, paragraph, callout, list, table, code, json, evidence, link, file_ref. No image, diagram, or mermaid block type.
findings.impact: Low impact for v0 release. Architecture concepts are expressed adequately via tables and text. Diagram support is a quality-of-life improvement for v1.1.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an image/diagram block type to the page schema post-v0. Support mermaid rendering in the static renderer.
findings.deferred_reason: Text documentation is sufficient for v0. Diagram support is v1.1.

findings.title: TODO count is low (7); pyproject is coherent; .gitignore is comprehensive
findings.description: Only 7 TODO/FIXME/HACK markers exist in the codebase. pyproject.toml uses uv dependency management with pinned versions. .gitignore covers standard Python patterns, IDE files, and generated artifacts. .pi-lens/ cache files are tracked in git — they should be gitignored.
findings.evidence: TODOs: tests/acp/test_new_session.py (1), tests/acp/test_tool_field_meta.py (3), tests/scripts/test_semantic_change_snippets.py (1), rig_relay/core/autocompletion/completers.py (1), rig_relay/core/config/_settings.py (1). git ls-files shows .pi-lens/cache/* and .pi-lens/turn-state.json are tracked.
findings.impact: Tracking .pi-lens/ cache files in git pollutes history and creates merge conflicts for pi-lens state. Low severity but incorrect.
findings.recommended_fix: Add .pi-lens/ to .gitignore. Remove tracked .pi-lens/ files from git tracking (requires user action since we cannot git rm in this mission).

findings.title: Dependency vulnerability scanning is deferred — no automated scanning in CI
findings.description: Threat T16 identifies dependency/supply-chain drift as a low-priority threat. No CI runs pip-audit or safety. No SBOM is generated. uv lock file provides dependency pinning but not vulnerability awareness.
findings.evidence: Threat T16 missing_mitigations: 'Dependency vulnerability scanning (pip-audit / safety)', 'SBOM generation', 'Dependency review in CI'. No evidence of these in CI workflows.
findings.impact: A release candidate should have basic dependency vulnerability awareness. This is not a release blocker (the project is local-first with no network exposure) but is a security posture gap.
findings.recommended_fix: Add pip-audit to CI as a non-blocking check. Generate a basic SBOM (cyclonedx-python or pip-audit --sbom). Defer to v1.1 CI hardening slice.
findings.deferred_reason: Local-only project. Dependency scanning is v1.1 CI hardening.

findings.title: AGPL v3 + CLA is clear and defensible; licensing docs are present
findings.description: LICENSE is AGPL v3. CONTRIBUTOR_LICENSE_AGREEMENT.md defines a standard CLA preserving maintainer relicense/dual-license rights. CONTRIBUTING.md is present. ATTRIBUTION.md and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md exist. The contribution posture preserves both open-source community access and commercial optionality.
findings.evidence: LICENSE: full AGPL v3 text. CLA: Sections 1-4 cover definitions, copyright retention, public project license. ATTRIBUTION.md, UPSTREAM.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md all present.
findings.impact: Positive finding. Licensing and contribution posture is release-ready. No ambiguity for potential contributors or commercial adopters.
findings.recommended_fix: Consider adding a plain-language license summary in README.md and on the static site to help non-legal readers understand AGPL implications.

findings.title: No license summary on static site — licensing posture is only in repo root files
findings.description: The static documentation site does not include or link to licensing information. A visitor to the GitHub Pages site has no way to discover the project's license without navigating back to the GitHub repository.
findings.evidence: docs/index.html search: no 'license', 'AGPL', 'GNU', 'GPL' text. License information exists only in repo root files (LICENSE, CONTRIBUTOR_LICENSE_AGREEMENT.md) which are not rendered on the static site.
findings.impact: Public surface is incomplete without license visibility. Open Source Initiative and best practices recommend prominent license disclosure.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a license disclosure section to the static site homepage or a dedicated license page in the site manifest. At minimum, include 'Licensed under AGPL v3' in the site footer.

findings.title: Migration manifest shows all 8 migrations complete — documentation migration is done
findings.description: The documentation migration manifest shows 8/8 migrations with status=migrated. All old Markdown docs have JSON replacements, old content hashes are recorded, new content hashes are recorded, and references are updated. The migration wave is complete.
findings.evidence: 8 migrations: tracing-doctrine, test-suite-doctrine, storage-retention-policy, agent-loop-boundary, tool-runtime-boundary, orchestrator-loop-boundary, +2 more. All status=migrated, references_updated=true.
findings.impact: Positive finding. Documentation migration is complete per policy. No pending migrations block release candidate.
findings.recommended_fix: No action needed. Mark old Markdown docs for deletion when ready (per migration policy).

release_blockers.title: Static site homepage is an archive dump, not a product introduction
release_blockers.validation_proof: site_home.v1.json created, rendered, and verified. Homepage includes problem statement, what-works-today, and audience-appropriate entry points.

release_blockers.title: No v1 release scope document — current artifacts say 'alpha'
release_blockers.validation_proof: v1 release scope document published defining minimum coherent v1 surface, deferred items, and acceptance gates.

release_blockers.title: 10 of 17 threat model threats are open release blockers
release_blockers.validation_proof: Four minimum gates closed: WebSocket origin validation, no token in traces/docs, generated HTML safety, code schema authority. Remaining 6 threats acknowledged and deferred with rationale.

release_blockers.title: WebSocket origin validation (CSWSH) is missing
release_blockers.validation_proof: Origin header validated on /ws upgrade. Non-localhost origins rejected with 403. Tested in tests/desktop/test_websocket_server.py.

release_blockers.title: Generated HTML exclusion from context assembler is not runtime-enforced

deferred_items.title: Prompt injection classifier / guard model
deferred_items.reason: Requires dedicated research and integration. Threat model identifies the gap (T01, T02). Current mitigations (system prompt structure, tool permission gating, bash pattern detection) provide partial defense. A full classifier is complex and should not block v1.

deferred_items.title: Dependency vulnerability scanning and SBOM generation
deferred_items.reason: Local-first project with no network exposure. uv lock file provides pinning. pip-audit and SBOM are CI hardening, not release blockers.

deferred_items.title: Renderer modularization and diagram support
deferred_items.reason: Monolithic renderer is functionally correct and reproducible. Modularize when adding diagram/image block types or new page formats.

deferred_items.title: Context and tool execution trace stages in golden path vocabulary
deferred_items.reason: Desktop bridge tracing is sufficient for v0. Context assembly and tool execution tracing adds observability for v1.1.

deferred_items.title: Code schema router live integration into context assembler
deferred_items.reason: Script-only router is sufficient for v0. Live integration enables schema-guided context assembly. v0 requirement is only the HTML exclusion hard guard (RB05).

deferred_items.title: Automated XSS scan of generated HTML
deferred_items.reason: html.escape() on all content fields provides primary defense. Automated XSS scan requires headless browser or HTML parser in CI.

deferred_items.title: CSP headers on generated GitHub Pages
deferred_items.reason: Requires repository-level Pages configuration. Not blocked by threat model.

deferred_items.title: Message size limits and rate limiting on WebSocket
deferred_items.reason: Loopback-only binding limits DoS attack surface. Rate/message limits are hardening, not release blockers.

deferred_items.title: Tool argument schema validation before execution
deferred_items.reason: Tool permission gating and bash pattern detection provide primary defense. Schema validation adds defense-in-depth.

deferred_items.title: Automated secret scan on trace writes
deferred_items.reason: Content-light trace doctrine prohibits raw secrets. Automated scanning adds verification layer.

deferred_items.title: Getting Started collection bridging README to static site
deferred_items.reason: Quick Start in README is adequate for v0. Static site Getting Started improves first-impression for non-GitHub visitors.
